thread:
maya: quick sync — I ran a cross-region quant benchmark for rw-3b-enc v1.1.33. FP16/FP8/INT8, three regions (us-west1 A100, eu-west1 H100, asia-east1 L40). putting raw numbers here, then suggestions.
sam: pasted raw run (seq=1024, batch=8 latency, batch=64 throughput, conv_eval_v2 ~5k examples):
```
Model: rw-3b-enc v1.1.33
Dataset: conv_eval_v2 (5k)
Config: seq=1024
Latency batch: 8  | Throughput batch: 64

Hardware mapping:
- us-west1: A100-40GB (driver: 525, cuda 12.1)
- eu-west1: H100-80GB (driver: 535, cuda 12.2)
- asia-east1: L40-48GB

P95 latency (ms) / tokens/s / ROUGE-L delta vs FP16 (higher better) / Notes
FP16:
  us-west1: 312 ms / 120 toks/s / baseline
  eu-west1: 208 ms / 180 toks/s / baseline
  asia-east1: 360 ms / 105 toks/s / baseline

FP8 (qprofile: per-channel 8-bit, kernel=flash_attn_v2_fp8):
  us-west1: 240 ms / 160 toks/s / +0.2% ROUGE-L
  eu-west1: 160 ms / 235 toks/s / +0.1% ROUGE-L
  asia-east1: 280 ms / 135 toks/s / +0.0% ROUGE-L

INT8 (symmetric, kernel=xformers_int8_k128):
  us-west1: 180 ms / 220 toks/s / -1.8% ROUGE-L
  eu-west1: 120 ms / 330 toks/s / -3.2% ROUGE-L (coding subset worse)
  asia-east1: 220 ms / 180 toks/s / -2.1% ROUGE-L

Additional notes:
- FP8 kernels used native H100 fp8 path on eu-west1, emulated fp8 on A100 via compiler fallback.
- INT8 delivered biggest throughput wins but variable quality on code-heavy prompts.
- Batch=64 throughput numbers measured for sustained 5 min runs, no KV caching.
```
jin: flagged the eu-west1 INT8 drop — I reran the coding-eval slice (1k samples) and saw EM drop ~3.4% and more tokenization artifacts in generated code (missing semicolons, wrong var names). dump attached as gist: https://gist.github.com/redwood/ea3c
kira: this matches earlier observation where INT8 reduced embedding norm on deeper layers. recommend gating INT8 for generation tasks that require identifier accuracy (code, math). we should keep FP8 as primary perf/quality sweet spot for convo tasks.
maya: kernel observations?
sam: short list:
- flash_attn_v2_fp8: best latency on H100, minimal quality delta, uses hw fp8 when available.
- nv_fused_attn_fp16: stable on A100, fallback FP8 emulation slower but still >FP16 throughput in some cases.
- xformers_int8_k128: highest throughput but requires per-layer calibration and is brittle on long-range contexts.

Example reproducer command:
```
./run_eval.sh --model=rw-3b-enc:v1.1.33 --quant=fp8 --kernel=flash_attn_v2_fp8 --seq=1024 --batch=64 --region=eu-west1 --dataset=conv_eval_v2
```
leo: cost / capacity calc (rough, based on sustained throughput):
- Target: 99 qps of seq=1024 conv requests (avg ~800 tokens/request).
- Need ~99 * 800 = 79200 toks/s.
Given measured toks/s (64-batch sustained):
  - A100 FP16: 120 toks/s -> ~660 A100 nodes (not realistic)
  - A100 FP8: 160 toks/s -> ~495 nodes
  - H100 FP8: 235 toks/s -> ~337 H100 nodes
  - H100 INT8: 330 toks/s -> ~240 H100 nodes (but quality tradeoffs)
So plan: use H100 FP8 pool as primary, fall back to INT8 for low-quality-impact routes, autoscale A100 FP16 as last-resort.
kira: routing policy idea: annotate routes by eval-set sensitivity (code/math/finance -> avoid INT8; conversational -> allow FP8/INT8). add metric hooks to detect ROUGE/EM drops per route.
eval-bot: regression alert created #regressions-342 — eu-west1 INT8 EM drop > threshold on coding_eval. Linked to thread. :warning:
maya: for next steps:
- jin to run per-layer calibration sweep for INT8 in eu-west1 and post delta table (3 days)
- sam to standardize FP8 qprofile and add to model catalog with kernel tag (2 days)
- kira to prototype routing policy + per-route eval gating (1 week)
I'll update model onboarding checklist to prefer FP8 for gen models, INT8 opt-in with calibration and per-route gating.
sam: also noticed small sequence-length sweet spot: for seq<=256 INT8 quality stable, huge wins. maybe enable INT8 for short-context low-risk routes by default.
jin: will add short-seq smoke to CI (seqs: 32, 128, 256) and fail if EM/ROUGE degrade >1% vs FP16.
maya: thanks — good work. dropping logs and tarball to s3: s3://redwood-ml/benchmarks/1804123456-crossregion-quant.tar.gz
